subject: SLA redlines - uptime triggering criteria & blackout/maintenance schedule
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@heliocorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioCorp Procurement <procurement@heliocorp.com>, J. Talbot <j.talbot@heliocorp.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA redlines - uptime triggers & maintenance blackout schedule

Marissa / team,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA/order form. We reviewed the SLA section and attached a short redline with two items we'd like to resolve before procurement can proceed:

1) Uptime trigger granularity: we prefer an "availability by region" definition (per-region windows) rather than a single global average. Our operations team needs outages isolated per region for incident response and regulatory reporting.

2) Maintenance blackout windows: we need a guaranteed quarterly blackout window where maintenance is not performed for our production tenants between 07:00-19:00 PT for three specified days each quarter; otherwise we require a rollback SLA and expedited notification.

We attached Helio_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf with inline notes. Would appreciate a proposed drafting approach and a timeline for legal to review. We are on a December/January procurement cadence and hope to finalize terms within 10 business days.

Best,
Samir Khan
Director, Cloud Ops — HelioCorp

Attachment: Helio_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf (annotated PDF, 2 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@heliocorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA redlines - uptime triggers & maintenance blackout schedule

Samir — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated PDF. We can take a small revision pass focused on the two items you flagged. Preliminary thoughts below so you have context before we produce redlines: 

- Uptime by region: we can include per-region availability buckets. We will need to confirm the set of regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1) that map to your traffic. This will change how credits compute (currently global aggregation).

- Blackout windows: we typically allow a rolling maintenance calendar with defined blackout exceptions. Your request (three specified days per quarter 07:00-19:00 PT) is reasonable but has operational cost impact for on-call and patching cadence. Two possible approaches:
  * Option A (preferred by ops): allow two standard blackout days per quarter + one customer-requested blackout day with 30 days' notice; maintenance outside those days can be scheduled with 72-hour notice.
  * Option B (customer-first): lock three fixed blackout days per quarter and require a rollback SLA for any non-exempt maintenance impacting availability.

Karthik / Rishi / Lauren — please review the two options below and advise on drafting language (I put a quick note in the attached MSA_annotated). Can legal accept per-region uptime buckets while preserving our current credit staircase? If not, propose alternative math. 

Next steps: we'll circulate a redline by EOD Friday after internal alignment. If Helio legal wants to jump on a 30-minute call, happy to schedule early next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Helio_MSA_annotated.docx (internal draft with option notes)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir@heliocorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA redlines - uptime triggers & maintenance blackout schedule

Marissa / Samir,

Thanks — quick legal/ops read and proposed drafting suggestions below. I'm putting the suggested language in-line for clarity.

1) Per-region availability: replace the existing definition of "Monthly Availability" with the following clause: 

"Monthly Availability (Regional): 'Monthly Availability' for Customer is measured per geographic region as defined in Appendix A. For each region, availability = 1 - (total region downtime seconds / total region uptime window seconds). Service Credits will be calculated on a per-region basis and applied only to the impacted region's usage for the billing month in which the downtime occurred."

Rationale: this avoids cross-region crediting leakage. It does change credit math; the settlement flow must summarize credits per region. Ops: please confirm logging hooks and reporting map to this definition.

2) Blackout/maintenance schedule: propose the following balanced clause (hybrid approach):

"Maintenance Windows and Customer Blackouts: Redwood will publish a 12-week rolling maintenance calendar. Customer is entitled to designate up to three quarterly blackout days per calendar quarter per region with the following constraints: (a) two blackout days may be designated without additional notice; (b) the third blackout day must be requested at least 30 days in advance. Redwood will not perform disruptive maintenance during designated blackout days. In the event Redwood performs emergency maintenance that affects availability during a designated blackout, Customer is entitled to either (i) a pro-rata Service Credit equal to 150% of the credit that would normally apply for the outage duration, or (ii) expedited rollback to the previous stable model release within 8 business hours at Redwood's expense, subject to operational feasibility."

Notes / asks: Rishi, can we commit to the 8-business-hour rollback window for model-serving changes and include an operational feasibility carveout? Also confirm whether 150% credit multiplier is acceptable commercially.

Samir — if the hybrid approach looks acceptable, we'll put it in redline form and circulate to Helio legal. If Helio prefers the strict Option B, be aware that locking three fixed blackout dates increases customer support and can impact our patching cadence; we'd want a pricing uplift or a narrower incident carveout.

Philippines ops: not included in this thread.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA redlines - uptime triggers & maintenance blackout schedule

Samir / Helio legal team —

Thanks for the quick review window. Per Karthik's suggestions, attached is a concise set of redlines that implement the per-region availability math and the hybrid blackout approach. Key points for Helio to confirm:

- Region list: please confirm the set of regions to include in Appendix A (we propose us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1).
- Blackout mechanics: confirm whether Helio accepts the hybrid approach (two default blackout days + one requested with 30-day notice) or prefers fixed days every quarter. If fixed days, we need to discuss a pricing uplift or an operational carveout.
- Emergency maintenance: please confirm that either the credit multiplier (150%) or the rollback at Redwood expense is acceptable. If Helio prefers both, call out which is give/ take.

Next steps: if you can confirm region list and blackout preference by EOD Monday, we will finalize redlines and circulate to our billing and ops teams for the final sign-off ahead of DocuSign. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call Monday 10:00 AM PT; otherwise we'll assume asynchronous review.

Appreciate the collaboration — we want to keep this moving to meet your procurement timeline.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
